Figure 2:Our network’s architecture for MEG-to-audio embedding alignment.
A 3-second, 208-channel MEG segment is processed by an interpretable front end: spherical-harmonic 3D spatial attention maps the sensor signals to 270 geometry-constrained virtual channels; a1×11\times 1unmixing convolution applies a learned affine transformation in this channel space; the subject-specific layer then projects the representation toKKinterpretable branches selected by the subject ID.
Each branch is passed through a depthwise temporal convolution with a 150 ms kernel, producing filtered branch-wise signals.
These signals are processed by a convolutional module withBBresidual convolutional blocks, where we evaluateB∈{0,…,5}B\in\{0,\ldots,5\}and useB=2B=2in the main architecture, followed by a convolutional head that outputs the MEG embedding aligned with the wav2vec audio embedding.

Figure 3:Retrieval accuracy as a function of the number of interpretable branchesKKand the number of convolutional blocks in the decoder.
For each configuration, Top-1 and Top-10 test accuracy are reported at the checkpoint with the lowest validation loss.
Accuracy increases sharply from very smallKKto approximatelyK=10K=10–2525, then enters a broad plateau; largerKKdoes not produce systematic gains and can mildly degrade performance.
Across decoder depths, the 0-block model is consistently weaker, while models with 2–5 convolutional blocks form a similar high-performing regime.
The main 2-conv,K=25K=25configuration lies on this compact high-accuracy plateau.

Figure 10:Feature-space compression of the target wav2vec representation.
The feature dimension is reduced using either a fixed PCA projection or a trainable linear projection optimized with the retrieval loss.
Learned feature reduction preserves retrieval accuracy over a wide range of dimensions, whereas PCA degrades substantially faster in the low-dimensional regime.

Figure 11:Temporal-resolution compression of the target wav2vec trajectory.
Temporal PCA, trainable linear reduction, local pooling, and global pooling methods are compared.
Unlike feature compression, temporal compression causes a clear performance loss, and global pooling collapses to near-chance retrieval.

Figure 12:Architectural ablations of the network’s front end.
Bars show the change in Top-1 and Top-10 retrieval accuracy relative to the full model.
The full spatial–temporal factorization performs best, with the largest degradation observed when subject-conditioned spatial mappings are removed.

Figure 13:Effect of temporal-filter support on retrieval accuracy. Points show
changes in Top-1 and Top-10 accuracy relative to the 150 ms default.
The one-sample condition contains no temporal context and acts only as
branch-wise scaling. All models used the same training seed and
validation-based checkpoint selection.
